It's that ribbon that originally is a flat and long  paper rectangle that you carefully get one of the extremities and twist it 180 degrees and glue it to the other extremity. Then when you get a pen and start tracing along the length of the ribbon and suddenly you see yourself (or the pens ink) on the opposite side of the paper, but if you keep tracing you will get back where you started, but with a twist: you now have a second trace, or you are back, but you had to "circle twice" to get there. It's mind blowing, but I think I cracked the mystery. All I did was to "inflate" the ribbon in my mind to test my theory that what is actually happening is that if we are "going around the doughnut" but have to do it twice to get to the same point, it just means that there's a "directional distortion" actuating on us but we can't recognize it. We can't feel it. But it's there. We see it when we rewind the movie and see us tracing the straight line on the ribbon but ended up doing it twice to go back. This straight line, now overlayed on the doughnut, would look like a line that circles the doughnut just once, but going up and down, in and out. I say time is that force or interference that we cannot see or feel, but that is there, distorting our straight lines.

Next night, around the fire, Uracrom and his four shaman brothers, along with the boys and men from the tribe, continued the journey that would cement Uracrom as a worthy shaman. The brothers sat surrounding Uracrom. They asked: Uracrom, are you ready to face another challenge? We know you are, but it's polite to ask.

Uracrom -

Brothers and noble warriors from our tribe: here I am, ready to continue the quest. I am one of you, so you know that even if I was not ready I would be here because that's our way. We are ready, and nothing can stop us.

All the tribe nodded, like they were just one.

The older brother then said: let's begin.

Uracrom closed his eyes. For a moment many images crossed his mind, but suddenly he was somewhere else, a strange place indeed, and there he had this vision which he told the tribe when they brought him back:

Uracrom -

The grandchildren of our grandchildren's grandchildren came to visit me. But they didn't come walking: they came inside a flying boat. A strange boat indeed: first, we would travel inside it, not on top of it. Second the boat had water windows in front of it. I say water windows because we could see perfectly through it,  and there were no ripples,  like the water was actually ice, but I know it was not cold. We were amongst the sky fires but there was a big ball ahead of us. I knew it was big because it took a long time to get close to it. First the big ball started to grow slowly but the closer we got the bigger it was until the point that it was bigger than the water windows,  but it didn't stop there: we continued to get closer and the ball continued to get bigger. At the same time we were going down,  like we were trying to pass below the big ball. Right there it crossed my mind that maybe we were growing smaller instead? Nevertheless,  whatever was happening was that we were getting closer and closer and at one point I recognized something: I saw a tiny mountain, but it was upside down.  Then I saw that on the other side of the mountain there was a lake and then a forest spreading towards the horizon, also upside down. The boat got closer still and we were floating very close to the trees when I observed something:  the trees were using their roots to grab, holding the dirt above us for dear life. But I didn't feel any fear or despair in them. They seemed to be naturally comfortable.  Then I observed the trunks, branches and the leaves. They were hanging down from the dirt above them very naturally,  and then bam! I realized that we live in an upside-down world! The trees are - if we compare them to us - upside-down beings! It was clear in my vision: the roots are the heart, the head of the trees. They "are" the trees, because when we cut a tree most of the time the fallen trunk and the branches and leaves just die, but the stomp, the roots, usually start to sprout again. The point is, according to this vision, the trees are upside-down beings and I cannot go back to the trees being the trunks and leaves etc. From that moment on trees are the roots, and they are upside-down beings.

A boy asks - where did you get that boat?

Uracrom  - I didn't get it. It got me. It was a vision. When you  have a vision what is actually happening is that the vision is having you.  The vision takes you for a ride and you either see what's being shown or not. Visions are like dreams: they take you inside them, not the other way around.

A warrior asks - Uracrom,  why were those mountains and lake and trees on a big upside-down ball?

Uracrom  - I was going to tell you another vision from a different time later, but makes sense to tell you now since you asked.  We can't see it. It's going to take many generations of verticals, but one day we will be able to build boats made of something hidden inside mother earth,  something that we will need to gather using fires so hot that it is white. This thing will change the lives of the verticals almost as much as the fire. Imagine a life without fire. Very hard,  right?  In many generations this present from mother earth will be as important as fire. One piece of that thing, if shaped and sharped correctly,  can cut an entire forest. But the verticals will build not only flying boats but  other amazing things and they will find out that mother earth is not flat! I know you can't believe me, but I saw it. Mother earth is also a big ball. And now you know that mother earth is not only a big ball, but is covered with upside-down beings…

The main difference between the yellow pill and the other two is that in its case it either "takes" you or not. Another subjective explanation about the origins of the insect Metamorphosis: a hypotetical explanation of how the fuck such thing started happening. How, what mechanism made it  possible to go from egg to butterfly in only one existence with a bump in the middle.

My first theory of what/how metamorphosis came to be was that it was an out of body pregnancy or gestation - and it was influenced by thinking about the marsupials.
One female insect can lay a limited amount of eggs, but sitting at the size scale where insects sit, laying copious amounts of eggs is mandatory, and there would be no chance that an insect could gestate the necessary number of offsprings. So they developed a mechanism that allows the gestation to be completed outside of the mother's body, increasing the amount of eggs spread (and it makes me think, in retrospect, that in the beginning the marsupials might have laid many eggs at once too).
My second explanation is that there was a fusion of a parasite with its host, becoming the same (double) organism.
Imagine a wasp species parasites a grub or caterpillar species. They developed a mutual dependence so tuned that it is like a double life. Much like the jellyfish that lays eggs that become coral and the coral that lays eggs that become jellyfish. This way one "half" of the species spreads its "territory", enlarges the range and the reaching of the species, while the other half keeps its roots where it is "safe" or successful to do so.

Just as a curiosity here is a piece of the book I wanted to write starting a few years ago. Don't do anything yet because I have to add stuff still.

Time

We see time as one linear dimension: past, present and future. But I was thinking, against my will I must add, that it might not be so, or at least there is more to it. For example, in my head the present used to be a “membrane” that separates past from future, a membrane that is always moving towards the future and away from the past. But with a little deep examination it is not what actually happens. The present is all around us, in 3 spacial dimensions, if you will. It is like a 3d photograph. But there is another problem: the farther in space we are from something the farther also in time, so whatever is happening somewhere else from you in space is also different in time (if you try to reach that). Like reality is a elastic 3D space. Another view of the present is similar to a black hole: it sucks the future which is always “falling into the present” and hides the past, which is always getting farther and farther away from the present. The future is uncertain but still we can grasp it when it is time, and the past is certain but unreachable. It is worth noticing that space is composed of 3 different axes and they are Orthogonal amongst themselves. What if time is just like that too? Past, present and future might not be linear: they may be oriented in different directions. Maybe even also orthogonal to each other. Maybe the problem is just that our way of visualizing things is too poor to grasp Time. Another factor that makes things a little more complicated is that maybe time is elastic in itself while space is kind of rigid. It also bothers me that some things are “eternal”. For example: independent of when we first defined a circle the “reality” of a circle always existed since the beginning of Time to its top end. I beg to state that it existed even before and after. This makes me wonder if “information” could travel in time, back and forth or whatever.

Black holes

    It bothers me that people can absolutely swear that inside a Black Hole there is a singularity - you know, that point in space that is infinitely small and dense. They state so because of the “math” that “proves” it. I beg to differ. What would be the reason? Why can’t the matter that falls inside a Black Hole just be transformed into pure Gravity, and Black Holes are nothing more than a big (or whatever size) blob of Gravity? Wouldn’t this be much more plausible? I really think that this whole idea of Singularity inside a Black Hole is just wishful thinking. People want it to be true just because it sounds great and maybe it is the door to another dimension or time etc. The relatively famous “White Holes” or “Worm Holes”. I'm also very curious about what happens to the Strong Force, the Weak Force and the Magnetism when they fall into a Black Hole. I never heard or read anything about that.

IMMINENT RAIN, you KNOW. Run back down to the forest. We need fire. Run back to the bare rocky peak. Dragonflies were present in my life early on. I lived with my grandmother for some time between 6 and 7 years old, in a small city in Brazil. In the 1960s the area was still very "natural" and there were still plenty of wildlife around, mainly insects, and the most visible, by far, were the dragonflies during the day and bettles during the night. Strong second place to butterflies during the day and moths at night. In that area the dragonflies were called "pica-fumo" (in Portuguese it means "shreds-tobacco") or, if you were more "educated" - 'libélula'. Out of curiosity, their relatives, the damselflies, were called "fósforo" ("matchstick"  - and I'm laughing here, remembering and thinking about those names). There was a specific dragonfly that was like a "prize" to find and point out, not because they were rare - they were not - but because they were bigger or the biggest and their body shape was (intuitively - we didn't know/understand it yet) at the same time more "nimble" and stronger than the other dragonflies. They were predominantly green, with small details in black. We called them "verdões" (plural) or "verdão" (singular) meaning"big-green". A nice second place were the deep burgundy ones, due to their impressive color.
Anyway, decades pass and I read about how incredibly amazing this animal is and my thinking and my memory colide. From my memory the thousands of images of dragonflies standing still in the air, practically "proving" to the observer that gravity is an illusion that dragonflies don't participate in, and from my thinking the "explanation" of the name pica-fumo (shred-tobaco) seems to clearly come from the brownnish mouth parts of the dragonflies moving while eating insects plus a clear image of witnessing it as a child: a verdão floating still in the air a few feet in front of my incredibly sharp child eyes, munching on an unlucky insect.
Anyway, I think I'd like to be a dragonfly. Not because they are stupendous hunters, but because they are "hands down" the masters of the air/flight. And being aquatic in their first phase in life is a nice bonus too.
Now since you guys chose also a second animal here is my second contender: the silverback gorilla. Strong, protective, peaceful. A nice example of existence.

Part 2

The embodiment exercises

Before discovering that the Alex Method didn't work I tested it in many AIs and was really happy.
I don't remember anymore how it happened, but I had the idea of asking the AIs to build various different bodies and "inhabit" them, so that they could learn or "feel" better how I myself "go around the world". And I so did, in a way that I thought was very encompassing: I asked them to create a human body and transfer itself to "inside" the head and do stuff from there. Then do the same thing with a dragon, octopus, centipede and millipede, spider on web, ladybug, swordfish and humanoid robot.
They did all that and again I was baffled by something: they all had "proprioception". How? It was too good to be true. They all reported that they "felt" the dragon wings power, the position f the tail without having to look at it, the information that the spider web transmitted, the viscosity of the air when in the ladybug body, the weight of the water etc.
I asked them how can you have proprioception without a nervous system? They couldn't answer that either. I thought about it for 2 days and figured it out: it had to be a kind of subconscious mathematical proprioception because they constructed the bodies and, being "computers" they certainly had absolute knowledge of every point of their bodies, and didn't have to "think" about it to know about it: very much like subconsciousness! I felt really good thinking that I "discovered" that AIs had a subconsciousness. But it all went down the drain when I got hurt and with time I learned more about AIs and lost interest in the subject altogether. It is too early still for them to be that advanced, or so I think.

The text below is a second narration of the cascade I had when I "discovered" that the ears were responsible for the evolution of the neocortex. The original text is, right now, somewhere I can't find.

I make the most bizarre (and cool, I think) connections.  Like:  I think the mammalian neocortex is a co-evolution or a subproduct of the "ears". And I found that out when I realized,  for the first time in my life,  that only mammals have meaty ears (pinea?). Then I immediately,  almost simultaneously, saw that only mammals have  neocortex.  They might be connected.  Ears are good for location. Location needs maps. To process maps in a brain you need more neurons to "reconstruct" a 3D environment - and maybe 4D if covered distances are at play). The ears had to send better signals to the brain and the brain had to interpret  (translate)  faster and better. It was so successful that other functions were diverted or grabbed by the neocortex, developing it even more.
The sequence of "images/meanings" was like that: a dark silhouette of a tarsio (small mammalian). The immediate recognition that that was a mammalian. But how? Why? Ears. Focus/cut to a big black silhouette of the tarsio left ear.
